entries.text: [intro] [kattribute] King [kname] [act] the Little Kingdom.  The former [former] achieved this feat by subduing the great dragon [dname] [dsaid] and claiming its great hoard of treasure.  He was able to achieve this victory with the aid of [weapon].  The king imprisoned his pet dragon in a great pit and built over it a great feast-hall, which became known as Wyrminghall, owing to the great wyrm contained below it.[paren] From his mighty hall the king founded [order], a small order consisting of His Majesty and his [knnumber] bravest vassals.  Although he paid nominal tribute to [gking], the lord of Wyrminghall ruled the Little Kingdom free of outside interference.

entries.text: [kbehavior], the Little Kingdom flourished, owing in large part to the fear of neighboring kings.  None dared make war against the realm, for fear that the last thing they saw would be a flash of [dcolor] scales shimmering in the bright sunlight, followed by an enveloping gout of [breath].  Another factor in the success of the kingdom was the influence of Queen [qname], wife of the Lord of Wyrminghall.  More shrewd than her husband, she was also known as [qreputation].  It was said that she first expanded the pits below Wyrminghall, adding a series of vaults to better protect the treasures of the realm and fiendish traps to guard the vaults as well as a series of dungeons and torture chambers for the benefit of local tax evaders.  Some tunnels below the hall are said to be the result of the dragon attempting to burrow his way out of bondage to the king.  Another tale suggests that some of the excavations originated from deep below the hall, made by the [deep] in an attempt to locate the gold and silver of the king.

entries.text: The first Lord of Wyrminghall enjoyed a long reign, as many as eighty winters by some accounts, before [kdeath]. [qfate] The son of the original king and queen of Wyrminghall, [2kname], ascended to the throne.  Barely adequate as a warrior and terrible at everything else, the second Lord of Wyrminghall's reign was short and disastrous, with most of the Dragon-Knights dying in battle against marauders or seeking service with a more worthy liege.  The second lord died without issue, leaving the tattered realm in the hands of his henchman Sir [3kname].  Eventually the hall was abandoned completely.  What remained of the Little Kingdom was absorbed into the Kingdom of Wessex.  Much later, [wizname], one of the founders of the Invisible School of Thaumaturgy at Christminster University, briefly took up residence in the now ruined hall.  No one knows when the dragon left Wyrminghall to return to its native [dhome], but all authorities agree the beast is long gone from the vicinity.

entries.text: The first Lord of Wyrminghall enjoyed a long reign, as many as eighty winters by some accounts, before [kdeath]. [qfate] The son of the original king and queen of Wyrminghall, [2kname], ascended to the throne.  Barely adequate as a warrior and terrible at everything else, the second Lord of Wyrminghall's reign was short and disastrous, with most of the Dragon-Knights dying in battle against marauders or seeking service with a more worthy liege.  The second lord died without issue, leaving the tattered realm in the hands of his henchman Sir [3kname].  Eventually the hall was abandoned completely.  What remained of the Little Kingdom was absorbed into the Kingdom of Wessex. No one knows when the dragon left Wyrminghall to return to its native [dhome], but all authorities agree the beast is long gone from the vicinity.
